metadata.scope: C++ metadata and symbol addresses; memory layout is not wire serialization order; virtual overrides need base-slot verification.

method: Read-only matched PE/PDB inspection and static instruction review; reference executable was not run. No code bytes or disassembly are included.

contracts.subject: fixed layer priority
contracts.behavior: Each of20 ability indices is resolved by searching LoadingScreen5, Editor4, Commands3, Spectator2, Base1, then CustomCache0 for the first ability whose type is not Unset1. Packet record order is not resolution priority.
anchors: PDB LayeredAbilities.mLayers: six Abilities, stride240; Ability stride12

contracts.subject: full replacement and duplicate records
contracts.behavior: The packet handler constructs a new LayeredAbilities, fills it from serialized data, and copies all six resulting layers into the player. fillIn first unsets every ability in every layer. Each serialized record then writes all20 abilities: allowed bits set the relevant bool/float, absent bits explicitly unset. A repeated layer record replaces the previous record including omitted abilities.
anchors: record callback RVA0xCD0CC0; absent bit branch RVA0xCD0D98
LocalPlayer::setAbilities RVA0x476CE40 -> base copy RVA0x1EFE80; full six-layer copy RVA0x1EFFCD..0x1F01CC

contracts.subject: unknown serialized layer
contracts.behavior: A serialized layer number at least6 is mapped to Base1 before applying its record.
anchors: RVA0xC4D759..0xC4D76D: unsigned16 comparison against6 and conditional Base1 selection

contracts.subject: permissions before explicit layers
contracts.behavior: After unsetting, fillIn sets the Base permission abilities before applying serialized records. Visitor0 disables indices0..7. Member1 enables0..5 and disables6..7. Operator2 enables0..7. Custom3 does not synthesize those grants. Any explicit Base record can unset these abilities through its allowed mask.

contracts.subject: float speeds and missing values
contracts.behavior: FlySpeed13, WalkSpeed14, and VerticalFlySpeed19 use independent allowed-mask bits and directly store their serialized floats, including zero. No set layer resolves to Abilities::INVALID_ABILITY rather than a previous packet value. The invalid ability object occupies a zero-initialized virtual data tail.
anchors: null return RVA0x1D77C0/0x1D782E; public symbol Abilities::INVALID_ABILITY RVA0x11D1BE68
PE .data begins RVA0X117DA000, raw size5414912, virtual size8772568; invalid object is beyond raw data

contracts.subject: fresh player defaults
contracts.behavior: The default ability definitions contain FlySpeed0.05f, WalkSpeed0.1f, VerticalFlySpeed1.0f. Perlin restores those defaults and clears previous flight/no-clip/instabuild state when reusing a connection/player/replay session. This reset is a Perlin lifecycle correction; its exact native connection scheduling is not inferred from the constructor.

contracts.subject: target identity
contracts.behavior: The packet handler looks up the player by the serialized ActorUniqueID and applies abilities to that found player. Perlin no longer interprets target0 as a broadcast to a different known local unique ID.
